In dense blackthorn hedges, many birds find shelter and room for their nests. The thorns keep enemies away. The **red-backed shrike**, a small songbird, likes to impale its prey on such thorns. The sloe is a **wild plum** and belongs to the **rose family**. It is related to the **damson** and the plum.

gewusst: Sloes often stay hanging on the shrub until winter.
With its suckers, a blackthorn shrub can overgrow whole banks.

teile.einleitung: A pest is an animal that damages plants, stored supplies or objects that are important to people. Whether an animal counts as a pest therefore depends on the human point of view.
wichtigste: The Spanish slug is regarded as especially troublesome in Swiss gardens.
The striped Colorado beetle eats potato leaves.
Aphids suck plant sap with a piercing mouthpart.
Their sweet excretion, honeydew, attracts ants.
The box tree moth comes from East Asia and strips box hedges bare.
The spotted wing drosophila lays its eggs in ripe cherries and berries.
The vole eats roots and tubers underground.

abschnitte.text: In nature there are no “good” or “bad” animals. Every animal looks for food. If in doing so it eats vegetables, fruit, forest or stored supplies, people call it a **pest**. Animals that eat pests are called **beneficial insects**, or beneficials, for example ladybirds, hedgehogs or birds. Many pests were brought in from other continents and have hardly any natural enemies here.

The **Spanish slug** is a large, orange to brown slug. It eats lettuce, seedlings and flowers and multiplies rapidly. In Swiss gardens it is regarded as especially troublesome. The **Colorado beetle** has yellow and black striped wing cases. It and its larvae strip the leaves from potato plants. It originally comes from North America.

**Aphids** pierce the plant’s vessels with a **piercing mouthpart** and suck the sugary sap. The sugar they do not need, they excrete as sticky **honeydew**. **Ants** love this sweet juice. They “milk” the aphids and in return protect them from enemies.

The green caterpillars of the **large white**, a white butterfly, eat big holes in cabbage leaves. The **box tree moth** is a moth from **East Asia** that was brought into Europe. Its caterpillars strip whole **box hedges** bare. Many gardens have therefore replaced their box with other shrubs.

The **spotted wing drosophila** is a small fly from **Asia**. Unlike other fruit flies, it lays its eggs in **ripe, healthy fruit** such as cherries, raspberries or grapes. The fruit then goes soft and rots. The **vole** lives underground and eats **roots, tubers and flower bulbs** there. Often you only notice it when a plant suddenly wilts.

gewusst: A ladybird and its larvae can eat thousands of aphids in their lifetime.
The Colorado beetle was so feared in Europe that in the past even school classes were sent out to the fields to collect it.

teile.einleitung: A dough is a soft mass of flour, liquid and other ingredients. It is used to bake bread, plaited loaf, cake or pizza. A lot of interesting things happen in dough while it is kneaded, rested and baked.
wichtigste: A simple bread dough is made of flour, water, salt and yeast.
Kneading makes the dough smooth and elastic.
A yeast dough rises while it rests and becomes about twice as big.
If the dough sticks, a little flour helps.
In Switzerland the dough is rolled out with a rolling pin called a “Wallholz”.
A loaf of bread has a crust on the outside and the crumb on the inside.

abschnitte.text: For a simple loaf, **flour**, **water**, **salt** and **yeast** are enough. No other ingredients are needed. For a plaited loaf, milk, butter and sometimes egg are added. For cakes and biscuits you use sugar and butter. Depending on the ingredients, very different doughs are made.

When you **knead**, the dough becomes smooth and elastic. Flour contains a protein called **gluten**. When kneaded, it forms a stretchy network. Later this network holds the little gas bubbles in place. If the dough sticks too much to your hands, you add a little **flour**, because flour soaks up moisture.

**Yeast** is made of tiny fungi. They feed on sugar from the flour and produce the gas **carbon dioxide**. The gas bubbles puff up the dough, and it becomes about twice as big. That is why a yeast dough is left to rest, covered. A **cloth** keeps it warm and stops its surface from drying out.

For cakes, tarts or pizza, the dough has to be thin. In Switzerland you roll it out with the **“Wallholz”**, which is called **“auswallen”**. In Germany the word for it is “Nudelholz”. A plaited loaf is made by braiding two or more strands of dough. Then the dough goes into the hot oven.

During baking, the surface of the dough becomes hot and dry. That is how the brown, crunchy **crust** forms. Inside, the bread stays soft and airy, and this part is called the **crumb**. In the crumb you can see the holes that formed as the dough rose. The heat in the oven kills the yeast, and the bread keeps its shape.

gewusst: The brown colour of the crust comes from a reaction between sugar and protein in the heat.
In many Swiss families, the “Butterzopf” (butter plait) is a traditional Sunday bread.
